I have farmed cotton on this land for 40 years. I am 63 now and I live alone, so I do all the field work myself except for hiring a rotary tiller in spring and some help at harvest. My farm is only 4.1 mu, which means every yuan I spend on inputs is a real expense, but I learned the hard way that skimping on fertilizer costs more than it saves. Two years ago I cut back to save money and my yield dropped by nearly 100 jin per mu. On a small farm, a bad harvest is a disaster, so I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than take that risk again.

This year I will sow cotton in spring, the same as always. I use improved seed — the kind my neighbors plant, not the old traditional types. I sow about 3 jin of seed per mu, which costs around 45 yuan per mu. For my base fertilizer, I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 100 jin of the 15-15-15 kind from the agricultural supply store, at 120 yuan per bag. That gives me 7.5 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphorus, and 7.5 kg of potassium per mu. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, I topdress with half a bag of urea, about 25 jin per mu, because the plants need extra nitrogen to keep the bolls from dropping. The urea adds another 5.5 kg of nitrogen per mu. In total I put down about 13 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphorus, and 7.5 kg of potassium per mu.

I have my own well, so I irrigate three times: once after sowing if the spring is dry, once at full flower, and once when the bolls are filling. Diesel for the pump costs money and moving the pipes is hard on my old bones, so three times is what I can manage, and it has always been enough.

Cotton pests are terrible in Quzhou. I spray insecticide 12 times from June to September, plus herbicide once before the rows close, and plant regulator twice to keep the plants from growing too tall and wasting energy. That is 15 pesticide applications in total. I mix the spray tanks myself. I would rather spray one extra time than wake up and find bollworms all over my field.

I rotary till every spring before planting. It costs 50 yuan per mu to hire the machine.

If the rain comes at the right time, I expect about 550 jin per mu — that is 275 kg per mu. On 4.1 mu, that gives me enough to cover my costs and live on for the year.
